name: Museum Kitzbühel
kurzbeschreibung: The Museum Kitzbühel in the historic Pfleggericht presents the world's largest collection of painter Alfons Walde, ski history, and a rooftop terrace.
oeffnungszeiten: Ganzjährig Di–So 10:00–17:00 Uhr (Do im Hochsommer bis 20:00 Uhr; Mo Ruhetag)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Museum Kitzbühel – Alfons Walde Collection is the leading municipal and art history museum in the legendary town of Kitzbühel. Housed within the historic Pfleggericht and the south-western defensive tower of the medieval town fortifications on Hinterstadt, the museum traces a captivating arc over several storeys from Bronze Age copper mining to Kitzbühel's rise as a world-famous winter sports capital and the classical modern era of Tyrolean painting. The heritage building is crowned by a spectacular 360-degree panoramic viewing terrace on the roof.

Alfons Walde & Winter Sports History

The crowning glory and international highlight of the museum is the world's largest permanent public collection of original masterworks by Kitzbühel painter and architect Alfons Walde (1891–1958). In light-filled galleries, more than 60 of his iconic oil paintings, graphic prints, and architectural blueprints are displayed: Walde's winter landscapes – including "Ascending Skiers", alpine pasture motifs, and portraits – decisively defined the visual imagery of Tyrol in the 20th century. A second major exhibition focus celebrates the history of alpine skiing: titled "Kitzbühel Ski Wonder", the display documents the sport's evolution from ski pioneer Franz Reisch (first descent from the Kitzbüheler Horn in 1893) to the inception of the legendary Hahnenkamm races in 1931 and the world-renowned Kitzbühel Wonder Team of the 1950s led by triple Olympic champion Toni Sailer, Anderl Molterer, and Christian Pravda. Historic wooden skis, racing suits, medals, and trophies bring alpine sports history to life, complemented by mining and civic history in the Gothic tower.

Visit & Arrival

The Museum Kitzbühel is open year-round Tuesday through Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (during peak summer in July and August extended every Thursday until 20:00; closed on Mondays). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): Adults €10.00, seniors and students €8.50, children and youths under 18 receive free admission! Discounts apply with the regional Kitzbühel Guest Card. Arrival by train: From the Kitzbühel Hahnenkamm railway station, it is approximately a five-minute stroll through Vorderstadt directly to Hinterstadt 32. By car: Via the B161 into Kitzbühel; parking is available at the Pfarrau car park or Stadtmitte.

Tips

The museum is comprehensively accessible for wheelchair users and strollers via a modern passenger elevator. Do not miss climbing up to the 360-degree rooftop viewing platform: from here, you enjoy an unforgettable vista over the colourful gables of Kitzbühel's old town, the Hahnenkamm with the Streif race course, and the Kitzbüheler Horn.
